concepts.explanation: Passing a point of no return. From Caesar crossing the Rubicon river to start a civil war.
A win so costly it amounts to a defeat.
A single fatal weakness in someone otherwise strong.
Something harmful disguised as a gift or benefit to get inside defences.
An action that unleashes many problems that cannot be undone.
Constant danger hanging over someone in a position of power.
A no-win situation where the rules trap you whatever you do. From Joseph Heller's novel.
A misleading clue that distracts from the real issue.
Conclusive proof of guilt.
Someone unfairly blamed to protect others.
A desperate last attempt with little chance of success. From American football.
A confrontation where no side can act without being destroyed, so nobody moves.
A sham trial with the verdict decided in advance.
An obvious problem everyone is avoiding mentioning.
Something given in exchange for something else. A favour for a favour.
Complete freedom to act as one wishes.
The final blow that ends something already dying.
Someone unwelcome, officially or socially. Used for expelled diplomats.
An unlikely event that conveniently solves a story's problem out of nowhere.
Pleasure taken in someone else's misfortune.
The defining mood or spirit of a particular era.
Trading your values or future for immediate gain. From Faust selling his soul.
An impossibly tangled problem, solved by a bold stroke rather than patience.
Endless, futile labour. From Sisyphus, condemned to roll a boulder uphill forever.
Nightmarishly complex, illogical and oppressive, especially bureaucracy.
Totalitarian surveillance and control of thought and language, from George Orwell's 1984.
Cunning and ruthless in pursuit of power, from the political writer Machiavelli.
A captive developing loyalty or affection toward their captor.
The simplest explanation that fits the facts is usually the right one.
Tiny causes leading to huge, unpredictable consequences.
A game theory puzzle where two people acting selfishly both end up worse off than if they had cooperated.
The study of strategic decisions. A zero-sum game is one where one side's gain is exactly the other's loss.
Manipulating someone into doubting their own memory or sanity.
A mechanism that triggers automatically if its operator dies or stops acting. Used as insurance in blackmail plots.
A cheap prepaid phone used briefly and discarded to avoid being traced.
Placing fake evidence to make an innocent person look guilty.
